headline: Global coverage highlights a world entering 2026 still shaped by conflict even as diplomatic actors and venues diversify
consensus: Multiple outlets agree that 2026 opens with significant armed conflicts and geopolitical strain still unresolved, prompting renewed debate over how and where diplomacy can be effective.

sections.subheading: A world still at war heading into 2026

sentences.text: The International Crisis Group published its annual list of ten conflicts to watch in 2026, warning that several flashpoints remain volatile.
Al Arabiya English similarly framed the start of the year as one in which peace remains elusive, describing a world still shaped by ongoing conflict.
The World Economic Forum argued that global cooperation matters most precisely because the world is, in its words, 'at war,' citing compounding risks across regions.
War on the Rocks examined last year's ceasefires and concluded that many amounted to pauses rather than genuine peace, reflecting a broader pattern of fragile conflict management.

sections.subheading: Diplomatic fallout from the Iran conflict

sentences.text: G7 finance ministers convened to discuss the economic risks stemming from the Iran conflict, alongside broader concerns about global trade fragmentation.
A separate analysis in Diplomacy and Law explored the wider implications of the Iran war for regional and international order.
Turkish President Erdogan, speaking at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum, warned of a global crisis and urged renewed diplomacy and regional stability.
Time Magazine argued that the traditional centers of diplomacy are losing relevance, contending that the world's new peacemakers are increasingly found in the Global South rather than in Geneva.

sections.subheading: Traditional forums still asserting a role

sentences.text: By contrast, Erdogan's remarks at the established Antalya Diplomacy Forum framed conventional regional diplomatic gatherings as the appropriate venue for addressing global crisis and instability.

sections.subheading: Emerging tools and training in diplomacy

sentences.text: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace analyzed a shift in China's approach to global artificial intelligence policy, describing it as a strategic pivot with diplomatic implications.
The Georgetown Journal of International Affairs made the case for leveraging science diplomacy specifically during times of conflict, as a channel that can remain open when political ties fray.
GIS Reports examined the diplomacy and realist politics surrounding the World Cup, framing sport as another arena where geopolitical interests play out.

On the academic and training side, the United Nations highlighted the role of women in diplomacy, News at IU profiled diplomat Cecily Brewer bringing real-world conflict-zone experience to students, Universiteit Leiden previewed its MIRD Gala focused on diplomacy in a changing world, and Boston University hosted a discussion on the Cambodia-Thailand conflict with scholar Sophal Ear.

disagreementGroups.stance: Traditional diplomatic centers (e.g., Geneva, established forums) are declining in relevance as the Global South takes the lead
Established regional diplomatic forums remain central venues for addressing global crises
